title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act sets rules and coordination requirements for using artificial intelligence in physical systems, such as robots and autonomous machines, to ensure they operate safely and reliably. It calls for developers, regulators, and other stakeholders to work together to create shared safety standards and prevent harmful or unsafe use.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The proposed amendment seeks to increase transparency and accountability for political ads that use AI-generated images or videos. It requires that any advertisement containing such AI-generated content must include a statement within the ad acknowledging that generative AI was used.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to shield elections from manipulation by AI-generated misinformation. It would impose transparency and accountability requirements on AI developers and enforce penalties to prevent deceptive AI from influencing voters and undermining democratic processes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes rules for overseeing AI systems that can modify themselves without external input. It aims to ensure these systems remain safe, transparent, and compliant with legal standards by setting up monitoring and reporting requirements.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on building new data centers specifically for AI workloads. It aims to address concerns about environmental impact, resource use, and ethical implications while additional research and guidelines are developed.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is intended to prevent artificial intelligence systems from acting in harmful or unpredictable ways. It establishes rules for developers and users to evaluate risks, enforce safety standards, and impose penalties if AI causes serious harm.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to oversee and investigate cybersecurity incidents and emerging AI threats, setting standards and coordinating responses. Its goal is to enhance national security by providing centralized accountability, policy guidance, and rapid action for risks posed by advanced AI and cyberattacks.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act seeks to ensure that artificial‑intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that directly benefit U.S. citizens, promoting innovation, job creation, and equitable access while safeguarding privacy and preventing bias. It proposes increased funding for AI research, the creation of safety and ethical standards, and programs to help workers transition into an AI‑driven economy.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: This act aims to regulate China's AI development, ensuring that AI systems are aligned with national security, ethical standards, and transparency in reporting. It requires companies to submit regular AI power reports detailing usage, performance, and compliance with regulatory guidelines.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 aims to ensure that only qualified medical professionals, not artificial intelligence systems, provide diagnostic and treatment services. It establishes regulations to limit AI involvement in patient care, protecting patients and maintaining the integrity of medical practice.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy proposes setting up a new office inside the President's Executive Office that will focus on monitoring and addressing risks from artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. This office aims to coordinate federal efforts and develop strategies to mitigate potential threats posed by these advanced technologies.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes guidelines to ensure that AI systems are rigorously tested for safety, accuracy, and ethical compliance before deployment. It requires researchers to document their methodologies, conduct thorough risk assessments, and collaborate with oversight bodies to maintain public trust in AI technologies.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to focus on protecting and hardening artificial intelligence systems against threats. It aims to coordinate efforts across agencies, develop best practices, and ensure the resilience of AI infrastructure for national security and public trust.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a framework for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating risks linked to artificial intelligence systems. It sets security standards and oversight mechanisms to protect users and critical infrastructure from potential AI‑related threats.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to guide and oversee AI policy. It defines the committee’s purpose, membership, authority, and responsibilities for promoting safe, responsible, and beneficial AI use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 creates a formal process for identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential harms from AI systems, requiring developers to conduct thorough risk evaluations before releasing their products. It also establishes a regulatory agency to oversee compliance, enforce safety standards, and ensure that AI technologies are deployed responsibly and transparently.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed legal framework designed to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems, ensuring they operate safely, transparently, and ethically. It aims to protect users and society by setting standards for AI accountability, bias mitigation, and human oversight, while fostering innovation and international cooperation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a federal law that aims to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies by setting standards for energy use, data center emissions, and hardware lifecycle management. It requires companies to measure and report their AI-related environmental impact, incentivizes the development of greener AI systems, and establishes penalties for non‑compliance.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a federal law designed to equip American students with the skills and knowledge needed to navigate an AI‑driven world. It requires states to develop AI education standards, provide teacher training, and ensure access to AI tools and resources across all K‑12 schools.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 establishes clear standards and testing requirements to ensure that AI systems developed in the United States are safe, reliable, and transparent. It creates a federal oversight body that monitors AI research projects, enforces these standards, and works to prevent harmful or untrustworthy AI technologies from being deployed.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to help protect critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. The program will test and evaluate AI tools for cyber defense, and the policy may include additional related actions to strengthen national security.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students from kindergarten through 12th grade with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate and understand artificial intelligence. The law would require schools to develop AI‑focused curricula, train teachers, and establish national standards to ensure that every student is prepared for a future where AI technology is ubiquitous.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to set clear rules and oversight for any artificial‑intelligence systems used in processing veterans’ claims, making sure those systems work fairly and transparently. It mandates the VA to implement safeguards, conduct regular audits, and report on AI decisions so that veterans’ rights and claim outcomes remain protected.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a proposed law that requires organizations developing or using artificial intelligence to disclose how their systems work, what data they rely on, and any potential biases or risks. It also establishes reporting and oversight mechanisms to ensure that AI deployments are transparent, safe, and aligned with public interest.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a nationwide campaign to raise public awareness about artificial intelligence, providing educational resources and outreach programs to inform citizens about AI’s benefits and risks. It aims to empower individuals with knowledge to make informed decisions and foster responsible AI use.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution stresses that AI systems must respect religious freedom and be guided by clear, authoritative texts. It also calls for transparency in AI operations so that users and regulators can understand and trust these systems.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a law designed to shield users from misleading AI systems. It requires AI developers to clearly label AI-generated content, provide accurate information about AI capabilities, and implement safeguards against manipulation.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress about how artificial intelligence systems are used to gather, analyze, query, share, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It focuses on the oversight and transparency of AI’s role in intelligence operations involving foreign surveillance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to boost AI skills across the workforce by investing in training and educational programs. It aims to ensure that students and workers are prepared for the growing demand in AI-related jobs and to support research that keeps the workforce current with emerging technologies.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act encourages developers to share AI code and data publicly to boost transparency and innovation. It sets guidelines and incentives that promote open collaboration, making advanced AI tools more accessible to researchers and businesses alike.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a law designed to stop companies from charging excessively high prices for AI services and from using AI tools to manipulate labor markets. It establishes penalties and regulatory oversight to ensure fair pricing and protect workers from automated wage exploitation.
